title: Primordial Particle System from random particles: ringed cells and spores form, persist and reproduce by budding and germination with no imposed rule; 63-111 persistent splits per seed, generation 2-3 (particle-identity tracker), and nothing forms at beta=0
summary: PPS at the published parameters (world.py, asynchronous updates, 5000 conserved particles, no feed, no division or death rule), from uniform random positions on 3 seeds to t=60000. ppstrack.py groups non-gas particles (>= 11 neighbours within r) into bodies linked within 5 units (>= 15 particles) and follows them by shared particle identity every 100 steps. 64-74 bodies on average in the second half, ring cells of 40-90 particles with an empty interior and compact spores of 15-25. Persistent splits (both daughters live >= 1500 steps and never re-merge with a sibling line; splits within 1500 of the end excluded): 102, 63 and 111 on seeds 0-2, max generation 3, 2 and 3, median parent size at split 68-75 particles. In 25, 12 and 36 of them both daughters reach half the parent's size within 3000 steps (germinating propagules). Strips of random generation-2 splits (img/) show cells budding spores, spores germinating into ring cells within ~500 steps, and cells breaking into spores. Control: beta=0 (no density-dependent turning) leaves the random particles frozen in place, with no cells (pack_beta0/sheet.png).

claims.statement: From uniformly random particles (seeds 0-2), PPS self-organizes into ring cells and spores that persist as particle bodies and reproduce without any imposed rule: 63-111 persistent splits per seed by particle identity, generation 2-3 after founders formed from noise, 12-36 per seed in which both daughters grow to at least half the parent's size.
claims.track: seed 0, the generation-2 split at t=39000 (img/splits_s0_gen2.png row 3): a 37-particle spore body splits into 34 + 22, and within 500 steps one daughter germinates into a ring cell that persists to t=40500

controls_run.S: pack_beta0/: beta=0, the same random start stays frozen (90 static clumps, no cells), so the structures come from the density-dependent turning

claims.bd_control: not applicable (particle world; no diffusion operator)

limits: The genealogy is heavily reticulate: the identity tracker records about as many merges as splits (1969-2292 each), most of them fragments that break off a ring and rejoin within a few hundred steps. The persistence rule removes those, but generation counts that pass through merges are uncertain, so confidence is low to medium. 'Split' mixes three things visible in the strips: cells budding a spore, a body splitting into two rings, and a cell dissolving into spores. labkit's grid tracker cannot follow these thin particle rings (persistent splits 0-2 in pack/), so the replication numbers rest on ppstrack.py. The ring is a geometric arrangement of the body's own particles, not an independent channel, so B is not claimed. Synchronous updates also make cells (sighting pack_sync), so the dynamics do not depend on asynchronous updating. The L/R handedness is the mirror of the counterclockwise convention (see the sighting).
